acceptance: The loader publishes either the result or the classified failure while holding the synchronization boundary before signaling waiters.
Every waiter observes the same published result or classified failure; no waiter can interpret an in-progress load as no answer set.
TPC-DS validation mode is supplied by run-scoped configuration and cannot leak between concurrent runs through module globals or cached objects.
Cached data is policy-independent, or a documented immutable policy identity is part of the key; tests prove concurrent exact, loose, skip, and disabled requests cannot contaminate one another.
Validation output distinguishes validated, no_answer_set, stream_not_reference_validated, provider_failed, and provider_timeout; a provider failure is never reported as a normal validation skip.
Fault-injection tests cover slow success, permanent absence, transient exception, timeout, retry, cache clearing, and multiple simultaneous waiters.
context: This extends the existing expected-results registry rather than adding another cache. Preserve the documented TPC-DS seed limitations; this item changes concurrency and provenance, not the statistical validation policy.
description:
ExpectedResultsRegistry signals waiting threads before publishing a successful load or cached permanent failure. TPC-DS expected-result objects also incorporate module-global validation mode while the cache key contains only benchmark and scale factor. Concurrent runs can therefore observe a false miss or reuse an answer object built under another run's policy. Make single-flight publication atomic and keep validation policy outside policy-independent cached answer data.

Decision boundary: cache immutable answer data by answer identity; apply validation policy at the requesting run boundary. Do not expand cache keys with mutable process-global state unless a narrower policy-independent cache is proven impossible.
